name: Ahijah
overview: Ahijah was a male figure known primarily for his role as secretary for King Solomon, a significant administrative position in the royal court. While his tribal affiliation and additional notes are not recorded, his service under Solomon highlights his importance in the governance of Israel during Solomon's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahijah means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the LORD. This proper name, mentioned in 1 Kings 4:3, does not appear to have been given directly by God but still carries spiritual significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ahijah was the father of Shisha, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahijah's significance lies in his trusted position as secretary to King Solomon, indicating his involvement in the administration and organization of the kingdom during a pivotal time in Israel's history. His mention in the biblical record underscores the importance of faithful service in the governance of God's people, contributing to the stability and prosperity of Solomon's reign.
